0 ![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/logo.png) ## DIagrams Through Ascii Art `ditaa` is a small command-line utility that can convert diagrams drawn using ascii art ('drawings' that contain characters that resemble lines like ```| / -``` ), into proper bitmap graphics. This is best illustrated by the following example: ``` +--------+ +-------+ +-------+ | | --+ ditaa +--> | | | Text | +-------+ |diagram| |Document| |!magic!| | | | {d}| | | | | +---+----+ +-------+ +-------+ : ^ | Lots of work | +-------------------------+ ``` After conversion using `ditaa`, the above file becomes: ![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/first.png) `ditaa` interprets ASCII art as a series of open and closed shapes, but it also uses special markup syntax to increase the possibilities of shapes and symbols that can be rendered. `ditaa` is open source and free software, released under the GPL license. ## Getting it For Ubuntu, there is a [package](http://packages.ubuntu.com/precise/ditaa). For MacOSX, you can install via [brew](http://brewformulas.org/Ditaa). ## Usage and syntax ### Command line You need the latest Java runtime (JRE) to use `ditaa`. To start from the command line, type (where `XXX` is the version number): `java -jar ditaaXXX.jar` You will be presented with the command-line options help: ``` -A,--no-antialias Turns anti-aliasing off. -b,--background The background colour of the image. The format should be a six-digit hexadecimal number (as in HTML, FF0000 for red). Pass an eight-digit hex to define transparency. This is overridden by --transparent. -d,--debug Renders the debug grid over the resulting image. -E,--no-separation Prevents the separation of common edges of shapes. -e,--encoding The encoding of the input file. -h,--html In this case the input is an HTML file. The contents of the 
 tags are rendered as
                                diagrams and saved in the images directory
                                and a new HTML file is produced with the
                                appropriate  tags.
 -o,--overwrite                 If the filename of the destination image
                                already exists, an alternative name is
                                chosen. Overwrite the image if it exists.
 -r,--round-corners             Causes all corners to be rendered as round
                                corners.
 -s,--scale              A natural number that determines the size of
                                the rendered image. The units are fractions
                                of the default size (2.5 renders 2.5 times
                                bigger than the default).
 -S,--no-shadows                Turns off the drop-shadow effect.
 -t,--tabs                Tabs are normally interpreted as 8 spaces
                                but it is possible to change that using this
                                option. It is not advisable to use tabs in
                                your diagrams.
 -T,--transparent               Causes the diagram to be rendered on a
                                transparent background. Overrides
                                --background.
 -v,--verbose                   Makes ditaa more verbose.
 -W,--fixed-slope               Makes sides of parallelograms and trapezoids
                                fixed.
```

### Syntax

#### Recognized shapes

The following shapes are recognized by `ditaa`:

- **Document** `{d}`: A shape with a wavy bottom edge
- **Storage** `{s}`: A cylindrical shape (database-like)
- **Ellipse** `{o}`: An oval/ellipse shape
- **Manual operation** `{mo}`: A shape with a slanted top
- **Decision** `{c}` ("Choice"): A diamond shape
- **Trapezoid** `{tr}`: A trapezoid shape
- **Input/Output** `{io}`: A parallelogram shape

Example:

```
+--------+   
|{d}     |   
|        |   
+--------+   
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/document.png)

#### Color

`ditaa` recognizes color codes:

- `cRED` - Red
- `cGRE` - Green
- `cBLU` - Blue
- `cPNK` - Pink
- `cYEL` - Yellow
- `cBLK` - Black

Example:

```
+---------+
| cBLU    |
|         |
|    +----+
|    |cPNK|
|    |    |
+----+----+
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/color.png)

Common edge separation (default):

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/separation.png)

No separation (with the `-E` option):

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/no_separation.png)

#### Dashed lines

Any lines that contain either at least one `=` (for horizontal lines) or at least one `:` (for vertical lines) are rendered as dashed lines. Only one of those characters can make a whole line dashed, so this feature "spreads". The rationale behind this is that you only have to change one character to switch from normal to dashed line, and vice versa.

Example:

```
----+  /----\  +----+
    :  |    |  :    |
    |  |    |  |{s} |
    v  \-=--+  +----+
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/dashed_demo.png)

#### Point markers

If `*` is encountered on a line (but not at the end of the line), it is rendered as a special marker, called the point marker. Example:

```
*----*
|    |      /--*
*    *      |
|    |  -*--+
*----*
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/point_marker.png)

#### Text handling

If the pattern ' o XXXXX' is encountered, where XXXXX is any text, the 'o' is interpreted and rendered as a bullet point. Note that there must be a space before the 'o' as well as after it.

Example:

```
/-----------------\
| Things to do    |
| cGRE            |
| o Cut the grass |
| o Buy jam       |
| o Fix car       |
| o Make website  |
\-----------------/
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/bullet.png)

#### HTML mode

When `ditaa` is run using the `--html` option, the input is an HTML file. The contents of the `
` tags are rendered as diagrams and saved in the images directory and a new HTML file is produced with the appropriate `` tags.

If the id parameter is present in the `
` tag, its value is used as the filename of the rendered png. Otherwise a filename of the form `ditaa_diagram_X.png` is used, where X is a number.

In this mode, files that exist are not generated again, they are just skipped. You can force overwrite of the files using the `--overwrite` option.

## License

`ditaa` is released under the GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0.

See LICENSE file for details.

import zlib, struct

def decode_png(filename):
    with open(filename, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()

    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])

    # Find IDAT chunk
    idat = b''
    pos = 8
    while pos < len(data):
        length, = struct.unpack('>I', data[pos:pos+4])
        ctype = data[pos+4:pos+8]
        if ctype == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[pos+8:pos+8+length]
        pos += 12 + length

    decompressed = zlib.decompress(idat)
    pixels = []
    line_bytes = w * 4 + 1
    for y in range(h):
        line = decompressed[y*line_bytes + 1 : (y+1)*line_bytes]
        row = []
        for x in range(w):
            r, g, b, a = line[x*4 : x*4+4]
            row.append((r, g, b, a))
        pixels.append(row)
    return w, h, pixels

w, h, pixels = decode_png('out.png')
print('Read image', w, h)

# Print ascii art representation of non-white pixels
for y in range(0, h, 2):
    row_str = ''
    for x in range(0, w):
        r, g, b, a = pixels[y][x]
        if (r, g, b) == (255, 255, 255):
            row_str += ' '
        elif (r, g, b) == (0, 0, 0):
            row_str += '#'
        elif (r, g, b) == (128, 128, 128):
            row_str += '.'
        else:
            row_str += '*'
    if row_str.strip():
        print(f'{y:2d}: {row_str}')
""}

import zlib, struct

def decode_png(filename):
    with open(filename, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()

    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])

    idat = b''
    pos = 8
    while pos < len(data):
        length, = struct.unpack('>I', data[pos:pos+4])
        ctype = data[pos+4:pos+8]
        if ctype == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[pos+8:pos+8+length]
        pos += 12 + length

    decompressed = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4
    stride = w * bpp
    raw = bytearray(w * h * bpp)

    def paeth(a, b, c):
        p = a + b - c
        pa = abs(p - a)
        pb = abs(p - b)
        pc = abs(p - c)
        if pa <= pb and pa <= pc: return a
        elif pb <= pc: return b
        else: return c

    src_pos = 0
    for y in range(h):
        filter_type = decompressed[src_pos]
        src_pos += 1
        scanline = decompressed[src_pos : src_pos + stride]
        src_pos += stride

        dst_line_start = y * stride
        for x in range(stride):
            filt = scanline[x]
            left = raw[dst_line_start + x - bpp] if x >= bpp else 0
            up = raw[dst_line_start - stride + x] if y > 0 else 0
            up_left = raw[dst_line_start - stride + x - bpp] if (y > 0 and x >= bpp) else 0

            elif filter_type == 1: val = (filt + left) & 0xff
            elif filter_type == 2: val = (filt + up) & 0xff
            elif filter_type == 3: val = (filt + (left + up) // 2) & 0xff
            elif filter_type == 4: val = (filt + paeth(left, up, up_left)) & 0xff
            raw[dst_line_start + x] = val

    for y in range(h):

            row.append((raw[idx], raw[idx+1], raw[idx+2], raw[idx+3]))

import zlib, struct

def decode_png(filename):
    with open(filename, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()

    w, h, bit_depth, color_type = struct.unpack('>IIBB', data[16:26])

    idat = b''
    pos = 8
    while pos < len(data):
        length, = struct.unpack('>I', data[pos:pos+4])
        ctype = data[pos+4:pos+8]
        if ctype == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[pos+8:pos+8+length]
        pos += 12 + length

    decompressed = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 3 if color_type == 2 else 4
    stride = w * bpp
    raw = bytearray(w * h * bpp)

    def paeth(a, b, c):
        p = a + b - c
        pa = abs(p - a)
        pb = abs(p - b)
        pc = abs(p - c)
        if pa <= pb and pa <= pc: return a
        elif pb <= pc: return b
        else: return c

    src_pos = 0
    for y in range(h):
        filter_type = decompressed[src_pos]
        src_pos += 1
        scanline = decompressed[src_pos : src_pos + stride]
        src_pos += stride

        dst_line_start = y * stride
        for x in range(stride):
            filt = scanline[x]
            left = raw[dst_line_start + x - bpp] if x >= bpp else 0
            up = raw[dst_line_start - stride + x] if y > 0 else 0
            up_left = raw[dst_line_start - stride + x - bpp] if (y > 0 and x >= bpp) else 0

            if filter_type == 0: val = filt
            elif filter_type == 1: val = (filt + left) & 0xff
            elif filter_type == 2: val = (filt + up) & 0xff
            elif filter_type == 3: val = (filt + (left + up) // 2) & 0xff
            elif filter_type == 4: val = (filt + paeth(left, up, up_left)) & 0xff
            raw[dst_line_start + x] = val

    pixels = []
    for y in range(h):
        row = []
        for x in range(w):
            idx = (y * w + x) * bpp
            if bpp == 3:
                row.append((raw[idx], raw[idx+1], raw[idx+2], 255))
            else:
                row.append((raw[idx], raw[idx+1], raw[idx+2], raw[idx+3]))
        pixels.append(row)
    return w, h, pixels

w, h, pixels = decode_png('shadow.png')

# Let's inspect colors around the right/bottom edge of the box (box is at x=25..65, y=35..63)
# Shadow should be around x=30..70, y=40..68
colors_found = set()
for y in range(35, 75):
    for x in range(25, 75):
        colors_found.add(pixels[y][x])

print('Unique pixel colors in box & shadow area:')
for c in sorted(colors_found):
    print(c)
""}

import time, zlib, struct

start = time.time()
w, h = 500, 300

    buf[i] = 255
    buf[i+1] = 255
    buf[i+2] = 255
    buf[i+3] = 255

    row_start = y * w * 4

        buf[idx] = 255
        buf[idx+1] = 0
        buf[idx+2] = 0

def write_png(width, height, rgba):
    def chunk(two, data):
        return struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + two + data + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(two + data) & 0xffffffff)

    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(height):
        raw.append(0)
        raw.extend(rgba[y*width*4 : (y+1)*width*4])

    compressed = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    ihdr = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, 8, 6, 0, 0, 0)

    return b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', ihdr) + chunk(b'IDAT', compressed) + chunk(b'IEND', b'')

png_data = write_png(w, h, buf)
elapsed = time.time() - start
print(f'PNG generated in {elapsed:.3f} seconds, size: {len(png_data)} bytes')

def draw_line_aa(width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, pixels, thickness=1.0):
    # Simple thick line rasterization with antialiasing
    dx = x1 - x0
    dy = y1 - y0
    length = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    if length == 0:
        return

    ux = dx / length
    uy = dy / length

    # Perp vector
    px = -uy
    py = ux

    min_x = max(0, int(min(x0, x1) - thickness - 1))
    max_x = min(width - 1, int(max(x0, x1) + thickness + 1))
    min_y = max(0, int(min(y0, y1) - thickness - 1))
    max_y = min(height - 1, int(max(y0, y1) + thickness + 1))

    half_t = thickness / 2.0

    for y in range(min_y, max_y + 1):
        for x in range(min_x, max_x + 1):
            # Distance to segment
            vx = x - x0
            vy = y - y0
            proj = vx * ux + vy * uy
            proj = max(0.0, min(length, proj))
            closest_x = x0 + proj * ux
            closest_y = y0 + proj * uy

            dist = math.hypot(x - closest_x, y - closest_y)
            if dist <= half_t + 0.5:
                alpha = 1.0
                if dist > half_t - 0.5:
                    alpha = 0.5 - (dist - half_t)

                alpha = max(0.0, min(1.0, alpha))
                if alpha > 0:
                    idx = (y * width + x) * 4
                    bg_a = pixels[idx+3] / 255.0
                    fg_a = (color[3] / 255.0) * alpha

                    out_a = fg_a + bg_a * (1.0 - fg_a)
                    if out_a > 0:
                        r = int((color[0] * fg_a + pixels[idx] * bg_a * (1.0 - fg_a)) / out_a)
                        g = int((color[1] * fg_a + pixels[idx+1] * bg_a * (1.0 - fg_a)) / out_a)
                        b = int((color[2] * fg_a + pixels[idx+2] * bg_a * (1.0 - fg_a)) / out_a)

                        pixels[idx+1] = min(255, max(0, g))
                        pixels[idx+2] = min(255, max(0, b))
                        pixels[idx+3] = min(255, max(0, a))

def draw_line_aa(width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, pixels, thickness=1.0):
    # Simple thick line rasterization with antialiasing
    dx = x1 - x0
    dy = y1 - y0
    length = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    if length == 0:
        return

    ux = dx / length
    uy = dy / length

    # Perp vector
    px = -uy
    py = ux

    min_x = max(0, int(min(x0, x1) - thickness - 1))
    max_x = min(width - 1, int(max(x0, x1) + thickness + 1))
    min_y = max(0, int(min(y0, y1) - thickness - 1))
    max_y = min(height - 1, int(max(y0, y1) + thickness + 1))

    half_t = thickness / 2.0

    for y in range(min_y, max_y + 1):
        for x in range(min_x, max_x + 1):
            # Distance to segment
            vx = x - x0
            vy = y - y0
            proj = vx * ux + vy * uy
            proj = max(0.0, min(length, proj))
            closest_x = x0 + proj * ux
            closest_y = y0 + proj * uy

            dist = math.hypot(x - closest_x, y - closest_y)
            if dist <= half_t + 0.5:
                alpha = 1.0
                if dist > half_t - 0.5:
                    alpha = 0.5 - (dist - half_t)

                alpha = max(0.0, min(1.0, alpha))
                if alpha > 0:
                    idx = (y * width + x) * 4
                    bg_a = pixels[idx+3] / 255.0
                    fg_a = (color[3] / 255.0) * alpha

                    out_a = fg_a + bg_a * (1.0 - fg_a)
                    if out_a > 0:
                        r = int((color[0] * fg_a + pixels[idx] * bg_a * (1.0 - fg_a)) / out_a)
                        g = int((color[1] * fg_a + pixels[idx+1] * bg_a * (1.0 - fg_a)) / out_a)
                        b = int((color[2] * fg_a + pixels[idx+2] * bg_a * (1.0 - fg_a)) / out_a)
                        a = int(out_a * 255.0)

                        pixels[idx] = min(255, max(0, r))
                        pixels[idx+1] = min(255, max(0, g))
                        pixels[idx+2] = min(255, max(0, b))
                        pixels[idx+3] = min(255, max(0, a))

    # Create shadow buffer
    s_buf = bytearray(width * height)

    shifted = [(p[0] + dx, p[1] + dy) for p in points]

    min_y = max(0, int(min(p[1] for p in shifted)))

        nodes = []

        for i in range(len(shifted)):

            if (p1[1] < y and p2[1] >= y) or (p2[1] < y and p1[1] >= y):

def parse_color_tag(tag):
    if tag in COLOR_MAP:
        return COLOR_MAP[tag]
    if len(tag) == 4 and tag.startswith('c'):
        r, g, b = tag[1], tag[2], tag[3]
        if all(c in '0123456789abcdefABCDEF' for c in (r, g, b)):
            return f"#{r}{r}{g}{g}{b}{b}".lower()
    return None

def hex_to_rgba(hex_str):
    if not hex_str:
        return (255, 255, 255, 255)
    hex_str = hex_str.lstrip('#')
    if len(hex_str) == 3:
        r = int(hex_str[0]*2, 16)
        g = int(hex_str[1]*2, 16)
        b = int(hex_str[2]*2, 16)
        return (r, g, b, 255)
    elif len(hex_str) == 6:
        r = int(hex_str[0:2], 16)
        g = int(hex_str[2:4], 16)
        b = int(hex_str[4:6], 16)
        return (r, g, b, 255)
    elif len(hex_str) == 8:
        r = int(hex_str[0:2], 16)
        g = int(hex_str[2:4], 16)
        b = int(hex_str[4:6], 16)
        a = int(hex_str[6:8], 16)
        return (r, g, b, a)
    return (255, 255, 255, 255)

def parse_color_tag(tag):
    if tag in COLOR_MAP:
        return COLOR_MAP[tag]
    if len(tag) == 4 and tag.startswith('c'):
        r, g, b = tag[1], tag[2], tag[3]
        if all(c in '0123456789abcdefABCDEF' for c in (r, g, b)):
            return f"#{r}{r}{g}{g}{b}{b}".lower()
    return None

def hex_to_rgba(hex_str):
    if not hex_str:
        return (255, 255, 255, 255)
    hex_str = hex_str.lstrip('#')
    if len(hex_str) == 3:
        r = int(hex_str[0]*2, 16)
        g = int(hex_str[1]*2, 16)
        b = int(hex_str[2]*2, 16)
        return (r, g, b, 255)
    elif len(hex_str) == 6:
        r = int(hex_str[0:2], 16)
        g = int(hex_str[2:4], 16)
        b = int(hex_str[4:6], 16)
        return (r, g, b, 255)
    elif len(hex_str) == 8:
        r = int(hex_str[0:2], 16)
        g = int(hex_str[2:4], 16)
        b = int(hex_str[4:6], 16)
        a = int(hex_str[6:8], 16)
        return (r, g, b, a)
    return (255, 255, 255, 255)

def parse_color_tag(tag):
    if tag in COLOR_MAP:
        return COLOR_MAP[tag]
    if len(tag) == 4 and tag.startswith('c'):
        r, g, b = tag[1], tag[2], tag[3]
        if all(c in '0123456789abcdefABCDEF' for c in (r, g, b)):
            return f"#{r}{r}{g}{g}{b}{b}".lower()
    return None

def hex_to_rgba(hex_str):
    if not hex_str:
        return (255, 255, 255, 255)
    hex_str = hex_str.lstrip('#')
    if len(hex_str) == 3:
        r = int(hex_str[0]*2, 16)
        g = int(hex_str[1]*2, 16)
        b = int(hex_str[2]*2, 16)
        return (r, g, b, 255)
    elif len(hex_str) == 6:
        r = int(hex_str[0:2], 16)
        g = int(hex_str[2:4], 16)
        b = int(hex_str[4:6], 16)
        return (r, g, b, 255)
    elif len(hex_str) == 8:
        r = int(hex_str[0:2], 16)
        g = int(hex_str[2:4], 16)
        b = int(hex_str[4:6], 16)
        a = int(hex_str[6:8], 16)
        return (r, g, b, a)
    return (255, 255, 255, 255)
